StackType.issue: PowerStackType.Single with the sim's on_stack overridden to `pass` citing it -- the census's 15-unit wrong-reasoning class (`py audit/tools/power_census.py stack`). Single means "Amount is hidden and is always 1" (PowerStackType.cs:10-13) and PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236) adds unconditionally with no StackType branch, so C# really reaches Amount 2. Dormant: nothing on either side reads Burrowed's Amount (it is a pure block-persistence marker), and monsters/hive/tunneler.py applies it once.

ShouldClearBlock.maps_to: powers.py:2288-2291 should_clear_block (hooks.py:613, consulted at combat.py:296 for enemies and player.py:157 for the player)
ShouldClearBlock.rationale: `base.Owner != creature -> true, else false` maps exactly to powers.py:2288-2291. This is the power's whole point (the Tunneler's block persists between turns) and it is right. Note the cross-reference: turn_structure gap G2 is about WHICH listener is the ShouldClearBlock preventer in each model (Barricade vs Sturdy Clamp) -- a listener-order question, not re-verdicted here, and inert for this power because it is the only preventer in a Tunneler fight.

AfterBlockBroken.issue: The trigger condition is right and the trigger POINT is right -- C# fires on the block actually breaking and cmds.py:78-81 reproduces the exact `Block <= 0 && blockedDamage > 0` semantics its own comment quotes (an exact break counts). Two divergences. (1) The STUN's follow-up state is dropped: C# calls `tunneler.GetStunned()` and THEN `CreatureCmd.Stun(base.Owner, tunneler.StillDizzyMove, "BITE_MOVE")` (BurrowedPower.cs:31-32), naming the state the Tunneler resumes on; the sim calls only `self.owner.get_stunned()` (powers.py:2298) and leaves the stun and the resume state to the monster. Whether that is observable is the Tunneler's record to settle, but it is the same shape as FlutterPower's -- where the follow-up-state re-roll turned out to be a LIVE wrong-RNG-stream gap (audit/records/power/flutter.json) -- so it is flagged, not waived. (2) ORDER: C# stuns first and removes the power SECOND (BurrowedPower.cs:32-33); the sim expires first (powers.py:2299) and then zeroes the block. Since AfterRemoved is what dumps the block, C#'s stun happens while the block is still there and the sim's after it is gone. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterRemoved.issue: C#'s AfterRemoved is `CreatureCmd.LoseBlock(oldOwner, 999999999m)` -- dump ALL the block -- and it runs on EVERY removal path, including the automatic strip when the owner dies (CreatureCmd.cs:533 then each power's AfterRemoved). The sim has no AfterRemoved analogue and hand-inlines the block dump at the single on_block_broken call site (powers.py:2300, comment `# AfterRemoved: LoseBlock(all)`). So a Burrowed removed any OTHER way keeps its block in the sim: notably on the owner's DEATH, where C# strips the power, fires AfterRemoved and dumps the block. DORMANT today only because the sim never strips powers on death either (see content-power-report-b.md section 3c) so no other removal path exists -- which means these two gaps cancel, and fixing either one alone re-opens this. Named trigger: any second Burrowed removal route, e.g. wiring ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath's default. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: Closed game-wide, re-verified 2026-07-26. EXECUTED: `py audit/tools/power_census.py visible` reports 0 IsVisibleInternal overrides of 260 files. That 260 is the .cs files DIRECTLY under src/Core/Models/Powers and EXCLUDES the 16 in Powers/Mocks/ (276 including them); a recursive `grep -rn IsVisibleInternal src/Core/Models/Powers/`, which does cover Mocks/, also returns 0 -- so IsVisible is provably always true for every power in the decompiled game, mocks included. CITATION FIX (2026-07-26 review fix pass): the property lives in src/Core/Models/PowerModel.cs, NOT under Models/Powers/ -- `IsVisible` is the non-virtual property at PowerModel.cs:150-160 and the overridable virtual is `IsVisibleInternal` at PowerModel.cs:167.
